([[New Hampton, New Hampshire]]) | college = [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] (2015–2017) | draft_year = 2017 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 24 | draft_team = [[Utah Jazz]] | career_start = 2017 | career_end = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2017|start}}–{{nbay|2018|end}} | team1 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years2 = 2017 | team2 = →[[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] | years3 = 2019 | team3 = →[[Capital City Go-Go]] | years4 = | team4 = | highlights = | bbr = lydonty01 | medal_templates = {{MedalCountry|{{flagu|United States}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2014 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|2014 United States]] | [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Tyler Robert Lydon''' (born April 9, 1996) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. ==Early life== Lydon attended Stissing Mountain High School in [[Pine Plains (town), New York|Pine Plains, New York]], then spent two years at [[New Hampton School]] in [[New Hampton, New Hampshire]].{{cite news|title=Tyler Lydon, former Stissing Mountain High School student, leaving Syracuse for NBA draft |url=http://www.dailyfreeman.com/sports/20170322/college-basketball-tyler-lydon-former-stissing-mountain-high-school-student-leaving-syracuse-for-nba-draft |accessdate=July 1, 2017|work=The Daily Freeman|date=March 22, 2017}} In 2014, he represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2014 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]] in [[Colorado Springs]]. He led the team in rebounds despite not starting any games en route to a gold medal.{{cite news |title=2014 FIBA Americas U18 Championship for Men |url=https://www.usab.com/history/u18-mens/ninth-fiba-americas-u18-championship-for-men-2014.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905200359/http://www.usab.com/history/u18-mens/ninth-fiba-americas-u18-championship-for-men-2014.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 5, 2015 |accessdate=20 May 2020 |work=www.usab.com |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |date=July 1, 2014}} Lydon committed to [[Syracuse University]] to play [[college basketball]].[http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2014/10/tyler_lydon_syracuse_basketball_recruit_is_a_confessed_country_boy_spurred_by_co.html Syracuse basketball recruit Tyler Lydon a confessed country boy spurred by competition] ==College career== As a freshman at Syracuse, Lydon averaged 10.1 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game.[http://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/sports/college/2016/03/29/shoeless-tyler-lydon-comes-age-syracuse/82395800/ 'Shoeless' Tyler Lydon comes of age for Syracuse][http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2016/05/tyler_lydon_could_become_oranges_next_star_syracuse_basketball_player_evaluation.html Tyler Lydon could become Orange's next star ] As a sophomore, he averaged 13.2 points, 8.6 rebounds and 1.4 blocks per game. After the season, he entered the [[2017 NBA draft]].[http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/18980325/tyler-lydon-syracuse-orange-enter-nba-draft Syracuse wing Tyler Lydon declares for NBA draft][http://www.poughkeepsiejournal.com/story/sports/2017/03/25/nba-within-reach-friends-say-tyler-lydon-wont-change/99468176/ With NBA within reach, friends say Tyler Lydon won't change] ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets (2017–2019)=== In the [[2017 NBA draft]], Lydon was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 24th pick in the first round, and was subsequently traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] shortly after being selected as a part of the deal for [[Donovan Mitchell]]. Lydon was assigned to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]] on October 23, 2017, before being recalled back to the Nuggets on November 8.{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets Assign Lydon/Transfer Craig, Morris to G League|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/assign-lydon-transfer-craig-morris-102317|accessdate=October 23, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2017}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.denverstiffs.com/2017/11/8/16624798/denver-nuggets-tyler-lydon-recalled-from-the-g-league|title=Tyler Lydon recalled from the G League|last=Gross|first=Gordon|date=November 8, 2017|work=denverstiffs.com|accessdate=November 19, 2017}} On March 3, 2019, Lydon was assigned to the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web|title=We have assigned Tyler Lydon to the Capital City Go-Go of the G League|url=https://twitter.com/nuggets/status/1102266965610061824|website=Denver Nuggets on Twitter|accessdate=March 10, 2019|date=March 3, 2019}} The Nuggets declined to pick up the third year option for Lydon's contract for the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]], making him an unrestricted free agent.{{Cite web|url=https://www.denverstiffs.com/2018/10/31/18048054/nuggets-decline-tyler-lydon-third-year-option|title=Nuggets decline third-year option for Tyler Lydon|last=Lewis|first=Daniel C.|date=2018-10-31|website=Denver Stiffs|access-date=2019-07-15}} On July 17, 2019, Lydon signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-tyler-lydon|title=Kings Sign Tyler Lydon|work=NBA.com|date=July 17, 2019|accessdate=July 17, 2019}} On October 21, 2019, the [[Sacramento Kings]] announced that they had waived Lydon.{{cite web|title=Kings Announce Roster Moves Wenyen Gabriel Elevated to Roster Spot, DaQuan Jeffries Added as Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-announce-roster-moves|date=October 21, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 21, 2019}} In July 2021, Lydon participated in [[The Basketball Tournament]]. He played for the [[Boeheim's Army]] and [[The Basketball Tournament 2021|won]] the winner-take-all $1 million prize.{{cite news |last1=Vasudevan |first1=Anish |title=4th-quarter push catapults Boeheim's Army to victory over Forces of Seoul, 65-53 |url=https://dailyorange.com/2021/07/boeheims-army-first-round-win-over-forces-of-seoul-in-the-basketball-tournament/ |access-date=6 August 2021 |work=[[The Daily Orange]] |date=24 July 2021}} He also indicated that he would retire as a basketball player after the tournament.{{cite news |last1=Ditota |first1=Donna |title=Tyler Lydon says this stint with Boeheim's Army will end basketball playing career
